question: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities are dealt under which schedule?
solution:
**The correct answer is 12th**

__
 
• The eleventh Schedule in the Indian Constitution specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 11th Schedule deals with the Power, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats, 29 subjects over which the Panchayats have jurisdiction.
 
• 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992:
 
 
• The institution of Panchayati Raj received a Constitutional guarantee, status, and legitimacy.
 
• The XI Schedule was added to deal with it.
 
• It also inserted part IX, containing Arts. 243, 243A.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• ​12th Schedule -

 
 
• It was added by the 74th Amendment Act of 1992.
 
• The powers, authority and responsibilities of municipalities are included in the Twelfth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This act gave constitutional status to municipalities in India.
 
• There are total 18 subjects in this schedule.
 
 
 
• ​9th Schedule -
 
 
• This schedule was added to the Constitution by the First Constitution Amendment Act, 1951.
 
• Under this, the methods of acquisition of property by the state have been mentioned.
 
• The matters included in these schedules cannot be challenged in court.
 
• At present there are 284 Acts in this Schedule.​
 
 
 
• ​4th Schedule -
 
 
• This schedule tells us about the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The number of members of the Rajya Sabha to be elected from each State/Union Territory is fixed by this Schedule.
 
 
 
• ​6th Schedule -
 
 
• The Sixth Schedule, passed in 1949, provides for the protection of the rights of tribals.
 
• This special provision has been made under Article 244 (2) and Article 275 (1) of the Constitution.
 
• The Governor has the power to constitute and reorganize autonomous districts.
